title: Token normalization — Code Similarity Search
description: Identifiers are normalized to ID and literals to LIT so that renamed variables still match. Keywords and operators stay literal because they carry the algorithmic structure. Normalization separates what the code does from what its author named things.

title: Shingle fingerprints — Code Similarity Search
description: Token streams are cut into overlapping n-grams (shingles); the set of shingles fingerprints the code. Jaccard similarity of shingle sets measures shared structure robustly. Shingling catches copied-and-pasted code even after edits.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: MinHash for scale — Code Similarity Search
description: MinHash compresses shingle sets into short signatures whose collision probability equals Jaccard similarity. Locality-sensitive hashing then buckets similar signatures so queries skip dissimilar code. This scales clone detection to billions of lines.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: AST-based comparison — Code Similarity Search
description: Parsing to an abstract syntax tree removes formatting and lets comparison work on structure. Tree edit distance or subtree hashing then measures similarity independent of layout. AST methods find clones that token methods miss across restructured code.

title: Type-1 to Type-4 clones — Code Similarity Search
description: Clone taxonomy runs from identical (Type-1) through renamed (Type-2) and edited (Type-3) to semantic equivalents (Type-4). Each type needs stronger analysis: text, tokens, trees, then program dependence graphs. Naming the clone type sets honest expectations for a detector.

title: Program dependence graphs — Code Similarity Search
description: PDGs link statements by data and control dependence, capturing semantics beyond syntax. Subgraph matching on PDGs finds Type-4 clones: different code, same behavior. PDG comparison is expensive but the gold standard for semantic clones.

title: Identifier semantics — Code Similarity Search
description: Split identifiers ('getUserName' to get/user/name) carry meaning; embedding them captures intent. Semantic similarity of names complements structural similarity of code. Name-aware search finds 'fetchCustomer' when querying 'getUser'.

title: Cross-language clones — Code Similarity Search
description: Algorithms recur across languages; normalized intermediate representations bridge syntax differences. Control-flow skeletons plus operator sequences transfer across Python, Java, and C++. Cross-language search finds the same algorithm wherever it was implemented.

title: Vulnerability clone search — Code Similarity Search

title: Embedding code models — Code Similarity Search

title: Incremental index updates — Code Similarity Search
